options: A PivotTable variant with extra formatting options
A separate transformation engine that connects to, reshapes, and loads data — distinct from formulas and PivotTables
Just another name for the SUMIFS and COUNTIFS functions
A macro recorder that only works with VBA
questions.explain: Power Query is its own transformation engine (branded 'Get & Transform' in Excel's ribbon) that connects to a data source, reshapes it, and only then loads the result — it's not a formula feature or a PivotTable variant.

questions.q: Where do you start every Power Query task in Excel?
options: Home tab > Editing group
Formulas tab > Function Library
Data tab > Get & Transform Data group
Review tab > Comments group
questions.explain: Every query begins with an option in the Get & Transform Data group on the Data tab — Get Data, From Text/CSV, From Web, From Sheet, and so on.

questions.q: What does the Applied Steps pane actually do?
options: Shows a live chart of your data
Records every transformation you make, in order, as a named and re-runnable step
Lists the keyboard shortcuts available in the Query Editor
Only displays error messages
questions.explain: Applied Steps is a running, ordered log of every transformation — remove a column, split text, change a type — each one saved as its own named step you can click, reorder, or delete.

questions.q: Why is Power Query more valuable than manually cleaning a refreshed data export by hand each time?
options: Because Power Query is faster at typing than a human
Because the recorded steps re-run automatically on Refresh, so the same cleanup applies to new data with one click instead of repeating manual work
Because manual cleaning is impossible in Excel
There's no real advantage — it's purely a matter of preference
questions.explain: Once a query's steps are recorded, refreshing the query re-applies every step to the current data automatically — turning a repeated manual chore into a single click.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's four-phase framework, what comes after Transform?
options: Connect
Refresh
Combine
Load
questions.explain: The four phases run Connect, Transform, Combine, then Load — Combine (Lesson 23) is where you merge or append multiple queries together, after transforming them individually.
